basics.name: Mudit Somani
basics.label: Software Engineer
basics.summary: I'm a passionate technologist with a drive for continuous learning and a curiosity for obscure or emerging technologies. I pride myself on my ability to dive deep into technical challenges and master new tools with focused intensity.

work.name: Cockroach Labs
work.description: Cockroach Labs is the creator of CockroachDB, the cloud native, distributed SQL database 338+ enterprises trust to run mission-critical applications.
work.summary: Developed internal AI-powered diagnostic platforms and cloud-native infrastructure for orchestrating stateful, durable AI agents.
highlights: Built Support Workspace, an internal platform enabling technical support engineers to inspect 100s of GBs of debug data via automated ingestion, agentic workflows for preliminary root-cause analysis, and an interactive AI copilot.

Integrated a suite of diagnostic and developer tools into Support Workspace, including a SQL editor and viewer, file explorer, pprof viewer, an interactive Docker container shell, and an agent skills collection.

Architected Kubernetes-orchestrated infrastructure for durable AI agents supporting isolated sandboxes, attached MCP servers, customizable agent harnesses, and stateful sessions backed by GCS buckets as memory stores.

work.name: Cockroach Labs
work.description: Cockroach Labs is the creator of CockroachDB, the cloud native, distributed SQL database 338+ enterprises trust to run mission-critical applications.
work.summary: Merged a production-ready feature into CockroachDB and owned the full development lifecycle, from initial design, testing and implementation to final merge and technical documentation
highlights: Added an OpenTelemetry-compatible log sink for CockroachDB to standardize observability and enhance system interoperability.
Introduced Protocol Buffers as a log serialization option, enabling a 20% reduction in network egress.
Created a OpenTelemetry processor to redact sensitive logs on-the-fly, reducing network throughput by 50%.

work.name: Google Summer of Code @ Dart
work.description: Google Summer of Code is a global, online program focused on bringing new contributors into open source software development.
work.summary: Created applications and tools to improve developer experience for the Dart programming language ecosystem along with stress testing the dart2wasm compiler and FFI capabilities.
highlights: Cross-compiled LLVM to make a WebAssembly version for libclang, enabling C/C++ source parsing and AST traversal directly in the browser without any servers or dependencies.
Developed FFIgenPad, a web app using SolidJS that generates Dart foreign function bindings from C headers entirely in the browser, without the need for any server-side processing.
Developed Dart AST explorer, a web app that allows you to visualize and explore the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of Dart code snippets in real-time.

work.name: ByteLeap
work.description: ByteLeap is a top-notch Product Engineering studio. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies and a deep understanding of user-centric design to deliver superior product engineering solutions.
work.summary: Interacted with multiple clients in a fast-paced environment to deliver software solutions on time.
highlights: Developed a full-stack LMS system with an admin panel and WYSIWYG editor to help train english teachers using React, NextJS, Prisma, and CockroachDB.
Built the SaaS platform for Athena copilot, a RAG-enabled AI assistant, using Clerk for authentication, NextJS, Sentry, Prisma and ShadCN UI Components.

volunteer.summary: Mentored an international student, providing technical guidance for the development of a terminal UI framework for the Dart programming language.
highlights: Conducted rigorous code reviews for over 35+ pull requests, ensuring adherence to project architecture, security standards, and best practices.
Managed the full project lifecycle, from initial proposal vetting and technical scoping to final delivery and documentation.

volunteer.organization: CRUX - the Coding Club of BITS Pilani, Hyderabad
volunteer.summary: Overseeing operations of the programming and computing club of BITS Pilani, Hyderabad which is responsible for the advocacy of coding culture in the campus.
highlights: Curated and led the development of 3+ open-source projects that were used by over 2000+ students on campus.
Streamlined onboarding process to happen every 2 months instead of once every semester to better capture student interest and reduce onboarding friction.
Organized workshops and mentored students on competitive programming, web development, and open-source contributions.

publications.name: Continual-learning for Modelling Low-Resource Languages from Large Language Models
publications.publisher: EACL 2026 - European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
publications.summary: Presents a parameter-efficient continual learning method that uses POS-based code-switching and a replay adapter to reduce catastrophic forgetting when adapting LLMs into SLMs for low-resource languages.

projects.name: localbox
projects.description: A fast, general-purpose sandboxed code execution engine built in Go for running untrusted code using Linux namespaces, cgroups v2, and Nix.
highlights: Built a concurrent sandbox pool atop Isolate with Linux namespaces, chroot, and host-shared cgroups v2 to enforce fine-grained CPU, memory, process, file, and network limits.
Integrated Nix to dynamically provision arbitrary compiler and runtime packages on demand alongside preconfigured multi-language engines.
Exposed a multi-phase execution REST API with OpenAPI schemas via Chi and Huma supporting multi-file mounts, custom workflows, and shell-free execution for accurate runtime metrics.

projects.name: lazycph
projects.description: A terminal UI competitive programming helper written in Go for managing and executing test cases directly from the terminal.
highlights: Built an interactive terminal interface with mouse and keyboard navigation using Bubble Tea, Bubbles, Lipgloss, and BubbleZone.
Implemented a local HTTP listener compatible with the Competitive Companion browser extension to automatically import problem metadata and sample test cases.
Designed a configurable language engine runner supporting both compiled and interpreted workflows, output diffing, and seamless editor integration.

projects.name: Demochain
projects.description: A serverless peer-to-peer blockchain network running entirely in the browser using WebRTC for interactive learning and demonstration.
highlights: Implemented a browser-native blockchain from scratch featuring SHA-256 Proof-of-Work consensus with configurable difficulty, nonce-ordered transactions, and mempool management.
Built decentralized peer-to-peer block and transaction gossip over WebRTC (Trystero) with Firebase signaling and compact binary serialization via CBOR.
Secured wallets, transaction signing, and block verification using Ed25519 cryptography in a reactive SolidJS and SolidStart web interface.

projects.name: FFIgenPad
projects.description: A web application that generates Dart FFI bindings from C header files directly in the browser using LibClang and WebAssembly.
highlights: Also built libclang-wasm as a separate module.
No server needed, runs completely in the browser.
Has a mini file-system to manage multiple header files and dependencies.

projects.name: LibClang WASM
projects.description: A standalone WebAssembly build of LLVM's LibClang enabling C/C++ source parsing and AST traversal in browsers and WASM runtimes.
highlights: Cross-compiled LLVM and Clang (up to v21) to WebAssembly using Emscripten, CMake, and Ninja with custom patches for virtualized executable paths.
Exported core LibClang symbols alongside memory management and Emscripten filesystem APIs as a modular ES6 library for seamless FFI interop.
Automated reproducible builds and prebuilt archive releases via GitHub Actions and Nix flakes.

projects.name: Lex
projects.description: A cross-platform lecture streaming and academic productivity platform built with Flutter and a companion Go backend, serving over 3,000 active student users at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad.
highlights: Built Multipartus, enabling students to search courses with BM25 full-text indexing, browse lectures across sections and semesters, and download timestamped slide decks.
Engineered a Go and Gin backend backed by SurrealDB and Logto OIDC authentication, rewriting encrypted HLS (m3u8) manifests to support AES-128 key delivery and multi-angle playback.
Developed a responsive cross-platform Flutter client across web, desktop, and mobile using MediaKit for video streaming and Signals for reactive state management.
